sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a restricted sample space.
[Asset: VennDiagram_Restricted] shows event B as the new universe.
Knowing B occurred changes our view of event A.
Consider the deck: If Red, is it a Heart?
P(Heart|Red) is thirteen over twenty-six, or point-five.
animations: Show title: 'Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability'. Color #FFFFFF.
Draw circle for Universe. Place event B circle inside Universe. Color #FF0000.
Draw event A circle overlapping B. Highlight intersection of A and B as 'A and B'. Color #00FF00.
Display MathTex: 'P(A|B) = P(A \cap B) / P(B)'. Color #FFFF00.
Use card deck example: Highlight Red (B) and Heart (A). Compute 13/26 = 0.5.

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
lecture_lines: Independent events do not influence each other's outcome.
Mathematically, P(A|B) equals P(A) for independent events.
Visualizing independence: two bubbles operating completely separately.
animations: Show title: 'The Concept of Independence'. Color #FFFFFF.
Draw two separate bubbles A and B. Size independent. Color #00FFFF.
Display MathTex: 'P(A|B) = P(A)'. Color #FF00FF.
Show coin flip 1: Heads or Tails. Show coin flip 2: Independent of flip 1. Color #00FF00.
Flashing equality sign in P(A|B) = P(A) to emphasize independence. Color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Introduction to Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem reverses conditional probability to update knowledge.
[Asset: FlowChart_Bayes] maps Prior probabilities to Posterior beliefs.
The formula: P(A|B) equals P(B|A) times P(A) over P(B).
We use this to infer causes from observed effects.
Testing for rare diseases makes this vital.
animations: Show title: 'Introduction to Bayes' Theorem'. Color #FFFFFF.
Display MathTex: 'P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}'. Color #FFFF00.
Show flowchart: Prior (P(A)) -> Evidence (P(B|A)) -> Posterior (P(A|B)). Color #00FFFF.
Draw bubble A (Disease) and B (Test Positive). Arrow from A to B. Color #FF0000.
Highlight P(A|B) as the final outcome. Color #00FF00.

sections.title: Putting It Together: A Real-World Scenario
lecture_lines: Robot R2 scans for a gold coin in a grid.
The prior probability the coin exists is point-one.
R2 is ninety percent accurate in its detection.
If R2 beeps, we apply Bayes' to update odds.
Prior knowledge is crucial for accurate real-world inference.
animations: Show title: 'Real-World Scenario'. Color #FFFFFF.
Display Grid with Gold Coin. P(Coin)=0.1. Color #FFD700.
Show Robot R2 sensor beep. 90% accuracy. Color #00FFFF.
Show Prior 0.1, Likelihood 0.9. Calculate updated probability. Color #FFFF00.
Display 'Updated Probability > 0.1'. Flash to emphasize learning from evidence. Color #00FF00.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Independence simplifies math; Bayes allows learning from evidence.
Independence is static; Bayes provides a dynamic updating mechanism.
Machine learning classifiers use these foundations for prediction.
animations: Show title: 'Summary and Conclusion'. Color #FFFFFF.
Show 'Independence' bubble = Static, 'Bayes' bubble = Updating. Color #00FFFF.
Connect concepts to 'Naive Bayes' for Spam filter. Color #FF00FF.
Final formula display: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Color #FFFF00.
